added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(p:=1/\varkappa=2+4/\beta\), \(L_m:=\log(2m)\),
\[
q_N:=\min\{1,N^{-\varkappa}\},\; A:=\ell q_N,
\; U:=L_m^{\varkappa}.
\]
These are proof-local abbreviations.  We first establish a distributional lower bound at an arbitrary splice amplitude, and then optimize it.

Fix \(c_0=3/4\).  Choose \(d=d_{\beta,D}>0\) so small that
\[
d\leq\min\{1/8,\beta/2,e\beta D/2,e\beta\log(3/2)\}.             \tag{22}
\]
For \(T\geq1\), set \(\delta=dT^{-\beta}\) and define
\[
S_0(y)=c_0y^{-4},\;
S_\delta(y)=
\begin{cases}
c_0y^{-4},&1\leq y\leq T,\\
c_0T^{-\delta}y^{-(4-\delta)},&y>T.
\end{cases}                                                       \tag{23}
\]
Both functions are nonincreasing and right-continuous, tend to zero, and have an atom of mass \(1-c_0\) at one, so they are genuine survivals supported on \([1,\infty)\).  For \(S_\delta\), take \(\alpha=4-\delta\) and \(c=c_0T^{-\delta}\).  Since
\[
\delta\log T=dT^{-\beta}\log T\leq\frac d{e\beta}\leq\log(3/2),
\]
condition (22) gives \(1/2\leq c\leq3/4\) and \(1\leq\alpha\leq4\).  Above \(T\) the Hall remainder is zero.  If \(1\leq y\leq T\), put \(z=y/T\).  The inequality \(e^u-1\leq ue^u\), followed by
\(\sup_{0<z\leq1}z^a\log(1/z)=1/(ea)\), gives
\[
\begin{split}
y^\beta\left|\frac{S_\delta(y)}{c y^{-(4-\delta)}}-1\right|
&=T^\beta z^\beta(z^{-\delta}-1)\\
&\leq T^\beta\delta z^{\beta-\delta}\log(1/z)
\leq\frac{d}{e(\beta-\delta)}\leq D.                            \tag{24}
\end{split}
\]
Thus both tails satisfy the support, index, scale, and Hall-envelope conditions of \(\mathrm{def{:}hall\text{-}class}\).

The tails in (23) agree through \(T\) and have common exceedance probability \(c_0T^{-4}\).  Conditional on exceeding \(T\), \(\log(L/T)\) is exponential with rate \(4\) under \(S_0\) and rate \(4-\delta\) under \(S_\delta\).  Direct integration therefore yields
\[
\begin{split}
\operatorname{KL}(S_\delta,S_0)
&=c_0T^{-4}\left\{\log\frac{4-\delta}{4}
+\frac4{4-\delta}-1\right\},\\
\operatorname{KL}(S_0,S_\delta)
&=c_0T^{-4}\left\{\log\frac4{4-\delta}
+\frac{4-\delta}{4}-1\right\}.
\end{split}                                                         \tag{25}
\]
Writing \(x=\delta/4\leq1/32\), the derivatives of
\(\log(1-x)+x/(1-x)\) and \(-\log(1-x)-x\) are respectively
\(x/(1-x)^2\) and \(x/(1-x)\).  Integration from zero proves from (25) that both directed divergences are at most
\[
C T^{-4}\delta^2,                                                   \tag{26}
\]
where \(C\) is numerical.

Let \(J=m/2\) and partition the cells into \(J\) pairs.  Give
\(\omega=(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_J)\in\{-1,+1\}^J\) the uniform product prior.  In pair \(j\), put \(S_\delta\) on the control arm of the cell selected by \(\omega_j\), and put \(S_0\) on every other control or treatment arm.  Draw the two potential losses independently conditional on \(X\), use the treatment probability in \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}probability}\), and set \(L=L(A)\) as in \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\).  Equations (22)--(24), together with the frozen uniform-cell and randomization assumptions, prove that every resulting law \(P_{\omega,\delta}\) lies in \(\mathcal H_{\beta,D}(m)\).  The chosen conditional independence of the potential losses is permitted because the class leaves their within-person coupling unrestricted.

For a feasible treated set, let \(H\) be the number of sign-selected heavy controls left untreated.  Treating all \(J\) heavy-control cells is feasible and produces the pure \(S_0\) mixture.  Every policy with \(H\) misses has mixture survival
\[
\frac HmS_\delta(y)+\left(1-\frac Hm\right)S_0(y).                \tag{27}
\]
The pure \(S_0\) log quantile is \(t_0=(\ell+\log c_0)/4\).  Suppose
\(b:=t_0-\log T\geq0\), and write the log regret in (27) as \(h\).  Substitution of \(y=\exp(t_0+h)>T\) into (23) and (27) gives the exact identity
\[
4h=\log\left[1+\frac Hm\left\{e^{\delta(b+h)}-1\right\}\right]. \tag{28}
\]
In particular, since \(h\geq0\),
\[
h\geq\frac14 g_z(H),\qquad
g_z(u):=\log\left[1+\frac um(e^z-1)\right],\; z:=\delta b.     \tag{29}
\]
For fixed \(z\geq0\), \(g_z\) is increasing and concave on \([0,m]\), and \(g_z(0)=0\).

We next show why unrestricted capacity reallocation cannot defeat (29).  Let \(K_j\) be the number of the \(n\) records whose cell lies in pair \(j\).  The vector \((K_1,\ldots,K_J)\) is independent of \(\omega\), and its entries sum to \(n=2NJ\).  Consequently at least \(J/2\) indices satisfy \(K_j\leq4N\).  Conditional on the count vector, the data blocks from distinct pairs are independent, and the product prior makes the posterior coordinates \(\omega_j\) independent.

Consider first a fixed realized data set.  In each pair a feasible action treats zero, one, or two cells.  Write \(r_j\) for the smaller posterior probability of its two signs, so a one-cell posterior-MAP action has conditional miss distribution \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(r_j)\), with \(r_j\leq1/2\).  A non-MAP one-cell action can only increase this Bernoulli parameter.  The capacity constraint implies that the number of two-cell actions is no larger than the number of zero-cell actions.  Pair one action of each type.  Their combined missed count is identically one.  Replacing them by one posterior-MAP treatment in each pair gives independent variables \(B_1,B_2\) with means at most \(1/2\).  For every fixed missed count \(R\) in the other pairs, Jensen's inequality and monotonicity give
\[
\mathbb E\{g_z(R+B_1+B_2)\mid\mathsf O_n\}
\leq g_z(R+r_1+r_2)\leq g_z(R+1).                                 \tag{30}
\]
Changing every remaining zero-cell action to a one-cell MAP action also cannot increase the conditional loss and respects capacity, because all paired two-cell actions have already been removed.  Iterating (30) proves that, among all feasible possibly randomized allocations, one posterior-MAP action in every pair minimizes the conditional expectation of the lower-envelope loss \(g_z(H)\).  Randomization cannot improve on the minimum of the deterministic conditional risks.

It remains to lower-bound the MAP error probabilities.  Given \(K_j=k\), the two sign experiments in pair \(j\) are product experiments with \(k\) observations.  By (26), their directed Kullback--Leibler divergences are bounded by
\[
CkT^{-4}\delta^2.                                                   \tag{31}
\]
Here the factor from the two cell labels and the control probability is at most one and is absorbed into \(C\).  We record an elementary testing inequality.  For two dominated laws \(Q_0,Q_1\), let
\(\rho=\int\sqrt{dQ_0dQ_1}\).  Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\(\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\leq\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\), while Jensen's inequality under \(Q_0\) gives
\(\rho\geq\exp\{-\operatorname{KL}(Q_0,Q_1)/2\}\).  Hence the equal-prior Bayes error obeys
\[
e(Q_0,Q_1)=\frac{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)}2
\geq\frac{\rho^2}{4}
\geq\frac14e^{-\operatorname{KL}(Q_0,Q_1)}.                       \tag{32}
\]
Combining (31)--(32), every pair with \(K_j\leq4N\) has its conditional-on-count Bayes error at least
\[
q:=\frac14\exp\{-C_1NT^{-4}\delta^2\}.                            \tag{33}
\]
After integrating the mutually independent pair data conditional on the count vector, the MAP error indicators are independent Bernoulli variables.  On the at least \(J/2\) low-count pairs their success probabilities are at least \(q\).  Thus their sum stochastically dominates a binomial variable \(Z\sim\operatorname{Bin}(r,q)\) with \(r\geq m/4\).  Equations (29)--(30) consequently imply, for every learner,
\[
2^{-J}\sum_{\omega}\mathbb E_{P_{\omega,\delta},n}h
\geq c\,\mathbb E g_z(Z).                                          \tag{34}
\]
This is the required distributional replacement for a mean-only Assouad step.

For clarity, the binomial expectation in (34) has an explicit two-regime lower bound.  If \(rq\geq1/4\), Paley--Zygmund and
\(\mathbb EZ^2\leq(rq)^2+rq\) give a numerical positive lower bound on
\(P\{Z\geq rq/2\}\).  If \(rq<1/4\), then
\(P(Z=1)=rq(1-q)^{r-1}\geq c rq\), because \(q\leq1/4\).  Adjusting constants over the overlap yields
\[
\mathbb E g_z(Z)\geq c\begin{cases}
\log\{1+q(e^z-1)\},&mq\geq c_2,\\
mq\log\{1+m^{-1}(e^z-1)\},&mq<c_2.
\end{cases}                                                         \tag{35}
\]
Thus (34)--(35) control the distribution of missed heavy cells from constant testing information through and beyond order \(\log m\), without assuming independent multinomial cell counts and without restricting the learner's capacity reallocation.

We now optimize a range that is sufficient for (21).  If \(N\geq1\), write
\[
T=(q_Nt)^{-1/\beta},\; \delta=dq_Nt,\;
1\leq t\leq q_N^{-1}.                                                \tag{36}
\]
Since \(Nq_N^p=1\), (33) becomes
\[
q\geq\tfrac14e^{-C_3t^p}.                                           \tag{37}
\]
Moreover, \(\log T\leq\log N/(2\beta+4)\).  The assumption
\(\tau\leq1/(8n)\), hence \(\ell\geq\log(8n)\), gives exactly as in the endpoint calculation for the fixed-amplitude splice
\[
b=\frac{\ell+\log(3/4)}4-\log T\geq c_\beta\ell.                  \tag{38}
\]
The affine difference has positive slope \(\beta/[4(\beta+2)]\), and its minimum over \(n\geq2\) is positive after reducing \(c_\beta\).  Therefore \(z\geq c_{\beta,D}At\).

Let
\[
s:=\min\{A^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)},U\}.                          \tag{39}
\]
First suppose \(q_N\max\{1,s\}\) is bounded above by a sufficiently small numerical constant.  If \(s\leq1\), take \(t=1\).  Equations (35), (37), and (38) give a lower bound \(cA\).  If \(s>1\), take \(t=\varepsilon s\), enlarging it to one if necessary, where \(\varepsilon=\varepsilon(\beta,D)>0\) is sufficiently small.  When
\(s=A^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}\),
\[
t^p\asymp A^{1/(1-\varkappa)}\asymp At;
\]
when \(s=U\), the inequality \(A\geq L_m^{1-\varkappa}\) gives
\(t^p\asymp L_m\leq CAt\).  Taking \(\varepsilon\) small uses \(p>1\) to ensure simultaneously that
\(C_3t^p\leq z/2\) and \(C_3t^p\leq L_m/2\).  Hence \(mq\geq c\), the first line of (35) applies, and
\[
\log\{1+q(e^z-1)\}\geq cAt.
\]
Together with the \(s\leq1\) case, this proves
\[
\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\geq cA(1+s)                                  \tag{40}
\]
whenever the right side is smaller than a fixed multiple of \(\ell\).

In the complementary saturation case choose \(T=1\) and \(\delta=d\).  If \(N<1\), (33) has constant testing information and (35) immediately gives \(c\ell\).  If \(N\geq1\), saturation in (39) implies \(q_NU\geq c\): this is immediate when \(s=U\), while when \(s=A^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}\leq U\) it follows from \(q_Ns\geq c\).  Consequently \(N\leq C L_m\).  Since now \(m\leq n\), the tail restriction gives \(L_m\leq\ell\).  By reducing the fixed \(d\) in (22), the testing exponent in (33) is at most a fixed fraction of \(d\ell\), whereas (38) with \(T=1\) gives \(z\geq c d\ell\).  The dense line of (35) then gives
\[
\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\geq c\ell.                                   \tag{41}
\]
Combining (39)--(41), and substituting the definitions of \(A,q_N,U\), is precisely (21).  Every lower-bound instance was verified in (22)--(24) to belong to the same \(\mathcal H_{\beta,D}(m)\), and the posterior comparison (30) covered every Markov-kernel learner in \(\mathfrak A_{n,m}\).  This completes the proof.
added_lemmas.justification: This proposition resolves the distributional missed-heavy-cell lower-bound step that a mean Hamming bound cannot handle.
added_lemmas.gap: CarpentierKim2015 supplies one-tail Hall testing rates but not the posterior capacity-exchange argument or the exact logarithmic loss of a growing selected mixture.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supplies the lower-side phase diagram that the open sharp-regret theorem must match with a full-class learner.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Tensorize two-arm Hall splices across paired cells at an arbitrary admissible amplitude, retain the exact logarithmic mixture loss, condition on the pair sample counts, factor the product posterior, and compare every feasible zero/one/two-cell capacity allocation with one posterior-MAP action per pair by concavity. A binomial lower-tail calculation followed by amplitude optimization gives the multiscale same-class lower envelope. The coordinatewise sorting-and-inversion learner remains a separate upper witness; equality of the two bounds is not part of this construction.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The previous handle described a hoped-for match. The distributional product-prior half is now proved, while the full-class capacity-aware upper match remains open, so the construction must distinguish those two facts.

proposed.statement: Determine \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\) up to constants depending only on \(\beta,D\) for every joint sequence \(n\to\infty\), even \(m=m_n\ge2\), and \(0<\tau_n\le1/(8n)\). The answer must identify every unavoidable logarithmic factor, give a necessary-and-sufficient joint-sequence criterion for \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\to0\), construct a computable \(\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{tail}}\) attaining the frontier, and prove a same-class lower bound against \(\mathfrak A_{n,m}\) that remains sharp through sparse-dominance, collective-contribution, and local-to-tied regimes. Express the answer as strict comparisons with both named baselines. In the dense reallocating regime \(m\to\infty\), \(m\log(2m)=o(n)\), and \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)\to0\), identify the maximal subregimes on which capacity averaging gives \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)=o\{\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)\}\) and the complementary subregimes on which the coordinatewise bound is unavoidable. Across every vanishing-regret regime, quantify the separation from \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{AW}}(n,m)\) rather than importing a regular-policy penalty.
proposed.justification: The product-prior missed-cell distribution is now controlled, exposing the remaining issue as a full-class capacity-aware achievability problem rather than a mean-only testing gap.
proposed.gap: CarpentierKim2015 gives an adaptive one-tail rate after the translation \(\beta_{\mathrm{CK}}=\beta/\alpha\), but it neither studies the stricter randomized product experiment with \(2m\) conditional tails nor proves a capacity-mixture oracle inequality. AtheyWager2021 concerns regular additive welfare and does not supply the missing extreme-mixture upper bound.
proposed.consumer: If completed, the theorem would give the non-nested upper-cost-quantile objective of OsamaZachariahStoica2020 a Hall-model extrapolation boundary; that paper is an objective anchor, not a class-inclusion or rate result.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct and analyze one computable capacity-aware learner over the full heterogeneous Hall class whose expected exact mixture regret matches the proved multiscale paired-splice lower envelope in every regime; or exhibit a harder same-class configuration and sharpen the lower envelope accordingly.
obligation.obstruction: The posterior capacity-exchange argument closes the lower-side distribution of missed heavy cells, but it has no upper-side analogue for data-dependent selected mixture weights. A natural-threshold plug-in controls average cell error but can select a severely underestimated heavy arm, while the presently proved uniform comparison prevents that event only by paying the familywise factor \([\log(2m)]^{\varkappa}\). Bounding the resulting weighted exponential tail-index errors without reverting to a coordinatewise maximum is the missing oracle inequality.
obligation.attempted: I conditioned on the fixed-sample multinomial pair counts, proved posterior factorization, showed by concavity that zero/double capacity reallocations cannot beat one MAP action per pair for the loss lower envelope, derived a binomial stochastic lower bound with error probability \(c\exp\{-CN\delta^{2+4/\beta}\}\), and optimized the splice amplitude through order-\(\log m\) information. On the upper side I tested the natural-threshold empirical minimizer and multiplicative core comparison; the former lacks control of selected heavy-arm underestimation and the latter collapses to the already-proved coordinatewise maximum bound.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The formal question remains valid, but its dependency and obligation metadata must record the proved multiscale distributional lower bound and remove the obsolete claim that the missed-cell distribution itself is still unknown.

proposed.comparator_claim: Equation (4) supplies a marginal upper-cost-quantile decision objective and its conformal limit can become uninformative when support information is inadequate; it is a non-nested consumer anchor, not a Hall-class inclusion or a rate engine.
Theorem 1 bounds constrained-policy regret for regular mean welfare by a policy-complexity and efficient-score scale.
The paper estimates a policy maximizing a fixed marginal potential-outcome quantile and derives nonstandard fixed-level asymptotics.

Its one-tail Hall results motivate the coordinatewise benchmark after the translation \(\beta_{\mathrm{CK}}=\beta/\alpha\). Each conditional tail here is a compact translated slice of that one-tail class, but the full randomized \(2m\)-tail causal experiment is a stricter product construction and the open capacity-mixture upper bound does not follow from their theorems.
The paper develops extreme-value inference for the average distribution of predetermined heterogeneous power-law observations.
Theorem 1 lower-bounds honest scalar tail confidence length by worst-case bias and the paper constructs a bias-aware interval.
Theorems 4.3 and 5.1 give process inference for extreme treatment contrasts over tail levels and fixed treatment pairs.
The manuscript derives finite-sample minimax-regret treatment rules for a fixed quantile with outcomes restricted to the unit interval.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The exact many-cell frontier remains open. The two affected rows must therefore record Carpentier--Kim as one-tail substrate and Osama--Zachariah--Stoica as a non-nested consumer, rather than promising an already-completed strict frontier match.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Match the proved multiscale paired-splice lower envelope with one computable full-class capacity-aware learner in every sparse, collective, and local-to-tied regime, or prove that another same-class configuration is harder.
open_obligations.obstruction: The distributional converse is no longer the gap. The missing step is an upper oracle inequality controlling data-dependent selected mixture weights under rare severe tail-index underestimation without using a coordinatewise maximum; the only verified learner pays \([\log(2m)]^{\varkappa}\).
open_obligations.attempted: I completed the fixed-sample posterior factorization, capacity exchange, binomial stochastic lower bound, and amplitude optimization. I then tried a natural-threshold empirical minimizer and an average multiplicative core comparison. Neither controls selection of a severely underestimated heavy arm, whereas imposing simultaneous control reproduces the existing familywise upper rate.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Put \(A_{n,m,\tau}:=\ell\min\{1,N^{-\varkappa}\}\) and \(L_m:=\log(2m)\).  The proved bounds now include
\[
c_{\beta,D}\min\!\left\{\ell,\;
A_{n,m,\tau}\left[1+\min\!\left\{
A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)},L_m^{\varkappa}
\right\}\right]\right\}
\leq\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)
\leq C_{\beta,D}\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau).
\]
The lower proof retains the exact identity
\[
4h=\log\left[1+\frac Hm\{e^{\delta(b+h)}-1\}\right]
\]
and replaces the mean-only Assouad step by a binomial stochastic lower bound for \(H\), valid after unrestricted capacity reallocation and for testing information from order one through order \(\log m\).  This proves the constant-information, intermediate, and familywise lower phases.  What remains unknown is whether a computable learner over the full heterogeneous Hall class attains this envelope, or whether a harder heterogeneous configuration raises it.

prose_updates.tldr: Capacity-constrained treatment choice at a beyond-sample loss quantile is governed by the inverse of a selected heterogeneous survival mixture. The proved results are a computable coordinatewise upper bound, the matching two-cell rate, and a sharper multiscale same-class lower envelope obtained from the exact distribution of missed paired heavy cells after unrestricted capacity reallocation. The exact all-sequence many-cell upper frontier and its if-and-only-if vanishing criterion remain open. The simultaneous-inference width converse and exact shrinking criterion also remain a separate open question.

project_justification.gap: Published fixed-level quantile-policy methods do not address extrapolated Hall tails. One-tail Hall theory gives a coordinatewise familywise benchmark, and regular policy-learning theory gives an additive-welfare benchmark, but neither supplies the capacity-aware oracle inequality needed to decide whether the new multiscale paired-splice lower phases are attainable over the full heterogeneous product experiment.
project_justification.niche: For each fixed even cell count, randomization identifies every policy mixture and capacity optimization is computable by sorting. Heterogeneous indices, local ties, empty observed cells, and growing mixture mass remain in the model; the new lower argument handles global capacity reallocations by posterior factorization rather than by a mean Hamming bound.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the generic full-class regret sandwich, the exact two-cell frontier, and a multiscale paired-splice lower envelope with constant-information, intermediate, and familywise-testing phases. It leaves the matching full-class capacity-aware learner explicit as the remaining regret problem and keeps confidence-width optimality separate from regret.

prose_updates.related_work: CarpentierKim2015 is one-tail statistical substrate, not a capacity-policy theorem. Each conditional tail in this note is a compact translated slice of its one-tail Hall class after the parameter conversion \(\beta_{\mathrm{CK}}=\beta/\alpha\), while the full randomized causal experiment couples \(2m\) such tails through a stricter product construction. The paired-splice converse transfers upward only to an explicitly defined superclass containing every constructed full-data law; an upper bound must be rechecked on that superclass and does not transfer from the splice. AtheyWager2021 and KitagawaTetenov2018 concern regular additive welfare, so their \(\sqrt{m/n}\)-type scale is a comparator rather than a tail-regret proof. WangZhouSongSherwood2018 and XiaZhangKong2026 occupy fixed-level quantile-policy identification or learning. OsamaZachariahStoica2020 supplies the non-nested marginal upper-cost-quantile consumer objective; it is neither a class-inclusion statement nor a rate engine for this Hall experiment. Its support-based conformal limit motivates the extrapolation question but does not establish the answer. Predetermined heterogeneous-tail pooling, scalar tail intervals, and fixed-pair extreme-treatment inference likewise do not resolve selection among capacity-constrained mixtures.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The prior mean-only obstruction is resolved: conditioning on fixed-sample pair counts preserves posterior independence, concavity removes any advantage from zero/double capacity reallocations, and a binomial lower bound controls missed heavy cells from constant through order-\(\log m\) testing information. The unresolved regret step is now exclusively achievability over the full Hall class: no proved learner controls data-dependent selected tail weights at the multiscale lower envelope without reverting to the coordinatewise maximum. Consequently the exact many-cell rate, every claimed logarithmic elbow, and the if-and-only-if vanishing criterion remain open. The confidence-width converse and exact shrinking condition remain separately open as well.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established claims are the fixed-cell Hall model and identification setup, sorting and inversion, Hall-core approximation, the local-dominance map, the generic coordinatewise regret sandwich, the two-cell matched rate, the simultaneous confidence upper system, and the new multiscale paired-splice lower envelope. The lower envelope applies to the same Hall class and all measurable randomized learners, but it is not yet a minimax equivalence. The exact many-cell capacity-aware upper frontier and the sharp confidence-width frontier remain open. No common tail index, fixed gap, density, nonempty realized cell sample, nuisance-rate assumption, or selection penalty is imposed. A paired-splice converse may be exported only to a superclass explicitly containing its full-data laws; the corresponding upper bound requires a separate proof.

statement_notes.justification: The lower-side missed-cell distribution and amplitude optimization are now proved; the remaining headline contribution is a matching full-class capacity-aware learner or a harder same-class lower configuration.
statement_notes.gap: CarpentierKim2015 supplies translated one-tail Hall machinery but no randomized product-class capacity oracle inequality, and AtheyWager2021 supplies no moving extreme-mixture rate.
statement_notes.consumer: Completion would give the non-nested upper-cost-quantile objective of OsamaZachariahStoica2020 an explicit Hall extrapolation boundary; that paper does not itself provide the boundary.

statement_notes.justification: This proposition replaces the invalid mean-only route with a distributional capacity-reallocation lower bound and exposes three explicit lower phases.
statement_notes.gap: No cited comparator supplies this paired-product posterior exchange or the exact logarithmic mixture-loss optimization.
statement_notes.consumer: It fixes the quantitative target that a future full-class capacity-aware learner must attain.
